title.narrative: ROAP/AFG03/24/Provision of shelter repair support and Seasonal winter assistance to vulnerable households affected by recent floods in Kabul and Nangahar provinces

description.narrative:
The takeover of government by the Taliban has triggered a dire humanitarian crisis, exacerbated by new decrees and laws that violate human rights, lead to poor governance and has contributed to a shrp decline in socioeconomic development.
Climate change, natural disasters, and migration especially forced returns from Pakistan has reduced economic opportunities and increased population in urban ares as people seek protection, better living environments, and employment opportunities. This rapid increase in urban population has increased the population's exposure and vulnerability to hazards.
Almost half of the Afghan population (23.7 million people), are estimated to need humanitarian assistance with 6.6 million needing emergency shelter and NFI (HNRP 2024). Recent floods have increased humanitarian needs and exacerbated the protection and shelter risks in areas of return, IDP and informal settlements. In addition, it is likely that returnees unable to return or remain in their place of origin will locate to informal settlements that lack basic and essential services such as water, sanitation, health, housing, protection, and other community infrastructures as sites of low-cost accommodation to access livelihoods and/or humanitarian services . Heavy rainfall, rapid snowmelt, and lack of vegetation in mountainous areas contribute to flooding risk, and strongly affect people living in urban areas (GFDRR & World Bank, 2017). On the other hand, the country struggles with a consecutive three-year drought-like condition, following the worst drought in 30 years in 2021/2022
social issues that include use of males for technical trainings for women, use of male enumerators during data collection, and long distances to distribution sites limit women participation in ES/NFI projects, thus impacting the assistance that women generally and women-headed households specifically can obtain and sometimes pose protection risk to the women (REACH and Shelter Cluster Afghanistan, Inclusion of women in ES/NFI programming, November 2023). Women with care obligations may also be excluded due to being unable to leave dependents
To address these needs, as per the Shelter Cluster winterization response plan 2024, UNHABITAT is proposing a project that will assess and select vulnerable households including NFI needs assessments through surveys, conduct a technical assessment to develop tailor made BoQs, designs and NFI needs for each individual selected households, and provide life-saving emergency winter shelter repair and winter NFIs (heating, clothing and blankets) to households affected by floods in Kabul & Nangahar provinces. The objective is to improve the living conditions of 645 households (398 household with other vulnerabilities, 150 women-headed households, 97 households with persons with disabilities) through provision of conditional cash assistance worth $550 per household paid in two installments (first $300 and second $250) for resilient major shelter repairs. Conditional cash for winter assistance will also be provided to these 600 households to support winter clothing for 7 people per household at a cost of $74 per household and sustainable heating system at a cost of $200 per household. In-kind winter assistance will also be provided in form of blankets to these 600 households to benefit 7 people per household at a cost of $57 per household. UN-Habitat will also provide women hygiene/dignity kits (4pkts menstrual pads, 4 tablets bathing soap, 2 pkts detergent/washing powder, multiple pairs (5) of underwear, 2 pkts sanitary napkins, 1 flashlight, 2 tubes toothpaste, 2 pairs of toothbrushes, 1 comb, and 1 plastic bucket) to 30 vulnerable households with most needy females. The conditional cash modality has been reached after discussing with the communities on how best they can be supported to complete the repairs on time. Overall, 4,516200 people (IDP’s, returnees, and host communities) will directly benefit from the project.
UN-Habitat has long-term agreements with AIB in Afghanistan and utilizes approved contracts for cash flow to beneficiaries. Using these modalities, UN-Habitat will use AIB bank to support with distribution of the cash to the beneficiaries to overcome challenges associated with cash distribution or banking systems. Transfers will be made in USD or Afghani (AFN) at the prevailing exchange rate.
UN-Habitat technical staff will continuously monitor the progress of the repairs and provide routine technical guidance and support to the households during the repairs to ensure compliance with quality standards and environmental and social safeguard issues. Post Monitoring Distribution will also be conducted to validated assistance provided.
